problems.problem: The gate has a real bypass that the selftest does not exercise. stripComments() is not string-aware, so a comment marker inside a string literal blanks real code and hides a leak. The selftest's only comment case ('quiet — prose about the rule inside comments') tests just one direction: prose inside real comments must stay quiet. It never checks that comment markers inside strings do not hide a leak. Two very ordinary shapes slip past. (a) An Express route glob such as '/files/*' anywhere above a leak opens a /* "comment" that runs to the next */ in the file. (b) A URL such as 'https://…' inside the 5xx body string turns the rest of the line into a // "comment", including err.message.

The bypass is latent, not historical.
problems.fix: This needs a gate change, which is outside the selftest author's remit, so escalate it. Make stripComments() skip string and template literals, using the same quote tracking responseStatementEnd() already has. Prove that the real tree still yields the same 10 sites. Then add two FAIL cases to the selftest, a route-glob string above a leak and a URL inside a 5xx body string, each asserting that the site is named.

problems.problem: Cleanup and hang robustness. The temp directory is removed only on the normal path and in abort(). An exception thrown while the cases array is built (linesOf throws 'fixture lacks …'), or inside a case's after() (JSON.parse of a malformed written baseline), leaves os.tmpdir()/server-error-leaks-selftest-*/ holding the patched gate and fixture tree. spawnSync also has no timeout, so a gate (or a SELFTEST_GATE_PATH mutant) whose statement walker never terminates hangs the selftest until the CI job times out.
problems.evidence: check-server-error-leaks.selftest.mjs: tmp is created at line 67. The cases array is built at lines 440-592, and linesOf is called eagerly inside it at lines 452, 528, 538, 563 and 564. problems.problem: The comment-line exclusion is only tested from the 'skip it' side. No failing case puts a violation on a line that also has a trailing // comment. problems.problem: The case 'an allowlisted site does not cover a new one in another file' does not test the file part of the allowlist key. problems.problem: Only the missing-shared/ case checks that the OK line is absent. The other failing cases check the exit code and the site names, so a gate that lists violations and also prints 'OK — all tenant columns are integer-typed' passes.

problems.problem: No case checks that the gate only reads the FIRST cell of a row (the `^` in `/^\| `([^`]+)`/gm`), even though the real doc already has a near-miss for it. In every fixture row, only the first cell has backticks. So a gate that takes any cell starting with a backtick as a file passes all 16 cases. That sloppier gate is wrong in both directions: it reports false stale rows, and it can count a baseline file as justified when the file is only mentioned inside another file's row, which is a false negative on the gate's main detection. The selftest header says its quiet cases are "the near-misses that real doc already has", and this one is missing.
problems.evidence: Mutant: a copy of the gate with the row regex changed to `/\| `([^`]+)`/gm` (only the `^` anchor dropped). Run via SELFTEST_GATE_PATH, the selftest exits 0 with 16/16 passing. The same mutant on the real tree exits 1 with "justification rows for files NO LONGER in the baseline: - getJobStatus". The cause is the deep-research-orchestrator row in docs/reports/tenant-isolation-justifications.md, whose third cell is "| `getJobStatus`; its comment states…". False-negative proof, in a temp fixture: baseline holds kernel-observability.ts and module-access-requests.ts; the only row is kernel-observability's, and its description cell begins with `server/routes/module-access-requests.ts`. The real gate exits 1 and names module-access-requests.ts. The mutant exits 0 with "2 source file(s) all justified".
problems.fix: Make `row()` emit later cells that start with a backticked token, the way the real doc does (for example `| `getJobStatus`; …`), so the quiet real-doc-shape case catches a gate that over-matches. Then add a FAILS case where an unjustified baseline file is mentioned only as a backticked path in a later cell of another file's row. It must exit 1 and name that file under 'baseline entries with NO justification row'.

problems.problem: No case covers the gate's end-of-file branch in the section regex `(?=\n## |$)`. Every fixture puts '## Resolved' and '## Standing follow-up' after the Justified section, so a doc where '## Justified entries' is the last `##` section is never tested. A mutant without `|$` survives. Its wrong output is a refusal ('section not found') rather than a silent pass, so this is a low-severity gap. It is still a coded branch the selftest never runs.
problems.evidence: Mutant: a copy of the gate with `(?=\n## |$)` changed to `(?=\n## )`. Run via SELFTEST_GATE_PATH, the selftest exits 0 with 16/16 passing. The real tree also passes under it, because the real doc has '## Resolved' after the table.
problems.fix: Add a quiet case whose doc ends with the Justified table, with no later `##` heading. Assert exit 0 and the 'N source file(s) all justified' line.

problems.problem: Under --strict-no-regression, which is the PR gate CI runs, no case checks which warning the baseline records, only that some warning appears or disappears. The only new-warning case goes from a clean baseline (warnings: 0) to one warning, so the count check alone (1 > 0) gives exit 1 and prints the same '0 new errors, 1 new warnings' message. The per-issue fingerprint check is never what decides a case. The real baseline (docs/reports/route-mount-audit-baseline.json) holds exactly 8 multi-use-prefix warnings, and the count stays at 8 when a PR removes one and adds another. In that swap, the fingerprint check is the only thing that fails the PR, and it is untested.
problems.evidence:
I ran mutants of copies of the gate in the scratchpad via SELFTEST_GATE_PATH. Each one passes all 20 cases ('20 passed — the gate fails on what it exists to catch'):
(mA) `const issueRegressed = newIssues.errors > 0;`, which drops the new-warning fingerprint check.
(mG) `return `${issue.type}|${key}`;` in fingerprintIssue, which drops the path, so every multi-use-prefix warning gets the same fingerprint.
(mK) `const warningCountRegressed = false;` also survives, because the two branches cover for each other.
Then a hand-built swap fixture: the baseline is written by the gate with /api/cmc mounted twice, and the tree mounts /api/ectd twice instead.
- Real gate: exit 1, 'Route mount regression detected: 1 warnings (baseline 1), 0 new errors, 1 new warnings'.
- mA: exit 0.
- mG: exit 0, 'Baseline delta: +0 new errors, +0 new warnings'.
For errors the selftest does cover this ('no-regression FAILS on a second duplicate the baseline does not record' kills a key-dropping mutant). It does not for warnings.
problems.fix: Add a no-regression swap case. Use `baseline: () => baselineFrom(CMC_TWICE)` with a tree that mounts a different non-gateway prefix twice (e.g. '/api/ectd' in two register-*.ts files) and no /api/cmc duplicate. Expect exit 1, 'Route mount regression detected', '1 warnings (baseline 1)', '0 new errors, 1 new warnings', and 'Prefix "/api/ectd"'. The count does not change, so only the fingerprint can fail this case, and it kills mA and mG. Optionally, to isolate the count check (mK), add a case whose baseline records the warning in issues but has `warnings: 0`. Expect exit 1 and '1 warnings (baseline 0), 0 new errors, 0 new warnings'.

problems.problem: The gate's mount regex captures eight kinds (use, get, post, put, patch, delete, options, head). The cases only exercise get, post and use. A gate that stopped seeing app.put, app.patch or app.delete passes every case. A duplicate, unguarded app.delete is the same defect as API-09.

The real tree has no put/patch/delete mounts today (grep over the default targets: app.use 330, app.get 16, app.post 4, all others 0), so nothing breaks now. A future duplicate destructive-method route would simply go unflagged.
problems.fix: Add one failing case for a write method other than POST. For example, two `app.delete('/api/documents/:id', ...)` mounts in different register-*.ts files, one without authenticateToken. Expect exit 1, 'Duplicate app.delete mount for "/api/documents/:id"', and both file:line sites.

problems.problem: The selftest header lists the --strict-no-regression fail-open only for a --baseline file that does not exist. It leaves out a more likely trigger: a baseline file that exists but does not parse. readJsonFileIfExists swallows JSON.parse errors and returns null, so a baseline with merge-conflict markers turns the PR gate into a silent pass. Even the 'Baseline delta' line disappears, because it is printed only when the baseline loads.
problems.evidence: I built a temp tree with the API-09 duplicate and a baseline.json containing '<<<<<<< HEAD ... >>>>>>> x' conflict markers, then ran `node scripts/ci/audit-route-mounts.mjs --strict-no-regression --baseline baseline.json`. Output: 'Errors: 1', 'Duplicate app.get mount for "/api/metrics"', and no Baseline delta line. EXIT=0. The header (lines 28-30) names only the missing-file case.
problems.fix: Extend the 'Not asserted' note in the header to cover a baseline that exists but does not parse (e.g. conflict markers): it fails open the same way, exit 0 with errors present and no Baseline delta line. Do not pin it as passing behaviour. This is a gate defect to raise, not a behaviour to lock in.

problems.problem: The selftest never checks where a router.param callback ends. If that slice runs to the end of the file, a guard inside a later handler gets credited to a router.param that only parses the id, and that silently clears unguarded routes. The selftest still passes 13/13 against that mutant. This is the same over-long-slice bug the gate header records as its historical regression, moved to the router.param branch, and it is not covered.

Running `SELFTEST_GATE_PATH=<mutant> node scripts/ci/check-org-path-param-guards.selftest.mjs` exits 0 with 0 failing cases. Concrete false negative, with the gate pointed at a temp tree containing `router.param('orgId', parse-only)`, then `router.get('/:orgId/a', … authorizeOrgAccess …)`, then an unguarded `router.get('/:orgId/b', …)`. The real gate exits 1 and names `GET /:orgId/b` (2 routes; 1 guarded, 1 not). Mutant D exits 0 with 'OK' (2 guarded, 0 not). Case 4 (parse-only router.param) cannot catch this because none of its routes contains a guard idiom.

problems.problem: ROUTE_RE explicitly accepts route paths in double quotes and in backtick template literals, but every fixture uses single quotes. A mutant that only detects single-quoted routes passes 13/13. Under it, a backtick-quoted org route becomes invisible to the gate: it is counted as 0 routes, which is worse than counted as guarded.

A fixture `router.get(`/v2/:orgId/b`, …)` with no guard: the real gate gives exit 1 and names `GET /v2/:orgId/b`. The mutant gives '0 route(s) take an org/tenant id…' and OK, exit 0. Prettier's singleQuote converts double quotes but leaves template literals alone, so the backtick form can occur in new code.

The gate header calls a false positive on a correctly guarded router.param 'the more corrosive failure', yet a regression that produces exactly that for orgId, organizationId, organization_id or tenant_id is not caught.

Case 4 uses router.param('orgId'), but its callback has no guard, so that route is unguarded under the gate and the mutant alike. Cases 5 and 8 only use 'tenantId'.

problems.evidence: Mutant A: `/router\.(?:get|post|put|patch|delete|all)\s*\(/g` changed to `/router\.(?:get|post|put|patch|delete)\s*\(/g`. The selftest exits 0 with 0 failing cases. There is no router.all in server/ today (grep is empty), so this is latent.

problems.problem: The gate never reads an entry's `reason`. A baseline entry with `{}` or with the --write-baseline placeholder `{ reason: 'TODO: …' }` suppresses an unguarded tenant route just as a justified entry does. Baseline `{"entries":{"server/routes/x.ts::GET /:orgId/b":{}}}` gives the same, exit 0 and 'OK'. Gate lines 189-193 consult only `key(f) in baseline`.

problems.problem: Not a selftest defect, but it must not stay buried in a selftest comment: the gate bug the selftest documents under 'Not a case' is real, and it is a live false negative. The router.param callback slice ends at the next ROUTE, not at the next param declaration as the gate's own comment (line 148) says. The real gate prints '1 route(s) … 1 guarded, 0 not' and 'OK', exit 0. The real tree has no router.param on a tenant id today (only projectId, plus the dynamic-name requireUuidParams format check), so current output is unaffected.

problems.problem: The comment-skip branch is only tested in one direction. The selftest checks that lines which are entirely comments are skipped (SSO_FIXED). No case checks that a leaky gate is still flagged when the same line carries a trailing comment. So if the skip is widened from 'line starts with // or *' to 'line contains //', that change passes all 15 cases, and the gate goes silent on the most common way people write a dev shortcut.
problems.evidence: I made a copy of the gate in the scratchpad, changing line 177 to `if (trimmed.includes('//') || trimmed.startsWith('*')) continue;`. With SELFTEST_GATE_PATH pointing at that copy, the selftest exits 0 with 0 failing cases. I then built a fixture with server/routes/auth.ts containing `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') { // local only: skip MFA`. The real gate reports it (FAIL, server/routes/auth.ts:2, exit 1).
